column2: Riding the borders with a patrol, [court_hero.GetTitledFirstName] was cornered in a ravine by a dozen raiders, beastmen by some accounts, bandits by others. [court_hero.GetSheHeCap] cut down half of them and the rest fled into the trees. The court can talk of nothing else, and the minstrels have already added a few more raiders to the tale.
We shall honour [court_hero.GetHerHim]!
A Sword of Battle for a fine warrior.
I could have done just as well.

A patrol riding the borders was ambushed on the forest road. [court_coward.GetTitledFirstName] wheeled [court_coward.GetHerHis] horse about and fled, leaving [court_coward.GetHerHis] men to die. Only two came home, and they have been telling everyone who will listen.
That was ill done.
Throw [court_coward.GetHerHim] in the dungeon!
Banish [court_coward.GetHerHim] for cowardice!
Back out there, and do not come back without a head.
[court_coward.GetFirstName] rides out again. [court_coward.GetSheHeCap] may win back [court_coward.GetHerHis] name, fail again, or not return at all.\n

The example of [heroknight_pupil.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName] has worked wonders on [heroknight_pupil.GetFirstName]. Your [heroknight_pupil.GetSonDaughter] climbed the tallest tower of the keep on a dare, faced down a stable hound twice [heroknight_pupil.GetHerHis] size, and now insists on riding at the head of every hunt.
Excellent!
[heroknight_pupil.GetSheHeCap] should be careful...

Hour after hour in the practice yard with [heroknight_pupil.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName], with horse, lance and blade, has turned your [heroknight_pupil.GetSonDaughter] [heroknight_pupil.GetFirstName] into a sturdy young [heroknight_pupil.GetManWoman] who rarely falls ill and never tires.

Your [heroknight_pupil.GetSonDaughter] [heroknight_pupil.GetFirstName] follows [heroknight_pupil.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName] everywhere with a wooden sword, and has started picking fights with every page and squire at court. [heroknight_pupil.GetSheHeCap] wins most of them.
This could be good, or bad...
That's my boy!
That's my girl!

[heroknight_pupil.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName] has taught your [heroknight_pupil.GetSonDaughter] [heroknight_pupil.GetFirstName] that a strong arm serves the weak, and that the law binds the lord as much as the peasant. Yesterday [heroknight_pupil.GetSheHe] made a guard return a loaf he had taken from a beggar.
[heroknight_pupil.GetSheHeCap] makes me proud!
Such notions are for fools!

My [Root.GetLordLady], your [heroknight_pupil.GetSonDaughter] [heroknight_pupil.GetFirstName] fell hard from [heroknight_pupil.GetHerHis] horse while practising at sword and lance with [heroknight_pupil.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName]. The physicians are with [heroknight_pupil.GetHerHim] now.
I hope [heroknight_pupil.GetSheHe] will come around!
This is a most grievous wound!

One of the eunuchs of the court has distinguished himself and caught the attention of my advisers. Though they are a jealous lot and loath to admit merit in others, even they cannot deny the promise of this young man.
Very well. Bring this man before me.
He should be scrubbing floors and watching over the women.

The eunuch is brought before me, and I can see at once the keen mind behind his eyes. His loyalty to me is beyond question: here is a man who cannot be seduced by the wiles of women or turned against me by ties of blood. Young as he is, he has already won renown for his skill in war.

The eunuch is brought before me, and I can see at once the keen mind behind his eyes. His loyalty to me is beyond question: here is a man who cannot be seduced by the wiles of women or turned against me by ties of blood. Young as he is, he has already won renown for his learning.
You will serve me well.
A great merchant caravan from distant lands has arrived at the gates. Its leader, a jovial man of enormous girth, begs in a strange accent for shelter from the elements for the night.
Very well. Let them in.
These peddlers may sleep in a ditch for all I care.
The caravan spends the night within your walls.

As evening falls, the fat merchant sits by the fire and regales the court with tales of his travels along the Ivory Road, of jade palaces and tiger-haunted jungles. His appetite seems bottomless, but not wishing to be a poor host, I order the servants to bring a second serving.
Tell us more of the fabled realm of Ind.

Dawn breaks and the caravan makes ready to move on. The merchant insists on leaving a gift in thanks for my hospitality. He barks a command in a foreign tongue and a young man steps forward. 'This eunuch will serve you well,' the merchant says. 'His loyalty to you, his new master, shall be beyond question.'
That is very kind. I accept your gift.
No, you may keep your servant.
Marshal
Spymaster
Steward
Chancellor
Lord Spiritual
councillor

A famous chronicler has come to court and offers to write the history of my house, from its first founder to my own glorious deeds. Such a work will cost a good deal, but it would carry our name down the centuries.
Give him my patronage.
I have no time for flatterers.

My young wife has taken a passion for romances. Tales of knights and their ladies, of forbidden love and stolen kisses: she reads every one she can lay her hands on, and her eyes shine when she speaks of them.
Then I will find her more to read.
That is her pastime, not mine.
Burn them! These books are the work of the Dark Gods!

[grumpy_priest.GetTitledFirstName] asks me to pay for a miracle play in honour of a local saint. The whole province would come to watch the saint's life and holy deeds acted out in the temple square, and the priests would remember my generosity.
It is for the glory of the gods!
If the temple wants it, the temple pays for it.
The peasants of my county want to hold a great carnival, with dancing, feasting and a fool crowned king for a day, and they ask me to pay for it.
We are rich. We can afford it.
They are just peasants.
A talented painter has come to court and offers to paint a great portrait of my late father to hang in the main hall for all to see.
It will look grand in the main hall.
A waste of money.
Your wife has her way, and the court follows.

Fine silks, slashed sleeves and towering hats are all the rage in the great courts of the world. My courtiers whisper that our own court looks dowdy beside them. Should I set a new fashion, and keep them busy keeping up with it?
Bring in the tailors!
There are better ways of spending the taxes.
My son [knocked_up_maid.GetFirstName] has got one of the servant girls with child. The whole household is talking of it, and the girl's family wants to know what I intend to do.
That's my boy!
He will take the child in as his own and avoid a scandal.
He gets a beating for meddling with servants.
He will go to the temple and atone.
My wife [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] is bored. She has heard of the latest fashions in the great courts, and nothing will do but that she have them too, at once, and in every colour.
My money is your money, darling.
Let us go to the temple instead, darling.
Shoo! This is my money you are talking about.
A herald famous across the land for his knowledge of arms and lineages offers me his service. He knows every great house and every quarrel between them, and would serve as a fine envoy.
Hire him.
Not interested.

A destitute noble from the court of my enemy has come to my gates. He has lost everything in this war and begs for a place at my court. In return, he says, he can give me a claim on lands of his former lord.
Welcome him to my court.
He may stay the night, no longer.

It is a shame that [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] keeps [court_holder.GetTitledFirstName] as [Root.Liege.GetHerHis] [Root.Liege.GetCourtPetitionJob]. I am the abler of us, and would serve far better!
I will petition my liege!
will hear our petition, and hopefully choose wisely
[From.GetBestName] claims that [From.GetSheHe] would make a better [Root.GetCourtPetitionJob] than [court_holder.GetTitledFirstName], and asks to be given the seat.
[From.GetSheHeCap] is my new [Root.GetCourtPetitionJob].
Give [court_holder.GetFirstName] a chance!
I rule in the [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName]!
will hear of our patience
My liege [From.GetBestName] is not happy with my work as [From.GetCourtPetitionJob], and is thinking of replacing me.
I must prove myself!
What can I do?
Enough time has passed. I deserve to be [From.GetCourtPetitionJob], and [From.GetTitledFirstName] will make me so!
I await [From.GetHerHis] reply eagerly.
I promised [From.GetBestName] a chance to become my [Root.GetCourtPetitionJob]. Now [From.GetSheHe] is petitioning me about it again.

My dear and trustworthy [Root.GetBestName],
I hereby grant you a seat on my council.

[From.GetBestName]
It is what I deserve.
By Any Other Name

My [Root.GetLordLady]! [courtier.GetTitledFirstName] has waited all morning by the hall door to catch me. "Half the court has a byname now, and the minstrels sing them. Would you give me one? Coming from you it would mean... well, it would mean everything."

My [Root.GetLordLady]! [courtier.GetTitledFirstName] hurries over with an armful of scrolls and a smudge of ink on [courtier.GetHerHis] nose. "I have read every book in the castle twice. Would you give me a byname, so the scholars of Altdorf and Nuln know whose letters they are reading?"

My [Root.GetLordLady]! [courtier.GetTitledFirstName] comes straight from the practice yard, mud to the knees and a notched blade on [courtier.GetHerHis] hip. "The men have names for each other. Give me one too, and I will make the enemy learn it."

My [Root.GetLordLady]! [courtier.GetTitledFirstName] slips out of a knot of chattering guests and makes [courtier.GetHerHis] way to me with a practised bow. "Every envoy I meet asks what they should call me. I would so like to have an answer from your own lips."

My [Root.GetLordLady]! [courtier.GetTitledFirstName] clutches a ledger to [courtier.GetHerHis] chest with ink-stained hands. "I have balanced the accounts of the household to the last penny. Would you honour me with a byname? Something... reliable."

My [Root.GetLordLady]. [courtier.GetTitledFirstName] is suddenly at my elbow, though I did not hear [courtier.GetHerHim] come. "People whisper about me. I would rather they whispered a name I chose. Or that you chose, of course."
You have earned a fine name.
Hm. What about...
Oh, you will have a name all right.
I have more important things to do.
Time to Go

A small crowd waits for me in the hall: hangers-on, poor cousins of cousins and knights without horses, most of whom I could not name if my life depended on it. Their spokesman bows. "We are leaving, my [Root.GetLordLady]. There is no room left at your table and less in your stables. Do we go with your blessing, and a little silver for the road?"
Go, and may Shallya keep you on the road.
Stay. I have changed my mind.

After a long council my head is full of grain prices and the cost of feeding my household. I sigh into my cup. [upbeat_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] slaps me on the back. "Cheer up, my [Root.GetLordLady]! Your hall is so full that the dogs sleep on the knights and the knights sleep on the dogs, and still nobody wants to leave. That has to say something good about you!"

At the end of supper [upbeat_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] calls me over to [upbeat_courtier.GetHerHis] table and raises a cup of [Root.GetAlcohol] to me. "To our host! Who feeds more mouths than the Emperor, and has to step over three of us to reach the privy every morning!" The whole crowded hall laughs and drinks.

Even shut away as I am, I hear the noise of my court through the door. [upbeat_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] is let in and bows. "My [Root.GetLordLady], we eat in shifts now, and sleep in shifts too. But nobody grumbles. We only want you to know that we are grateful for the roof."
Oh, but I like sleeping in the stables now and then!
There is strength in numbers, my friend. Remember that.
I simply enjoy your company, all of you.
More mouths, more hands for the work.
Every one of you matters to me.
You are my family. Of course there is room for you.
[invited_character.GetFullName] has arrived at your court, ready for employment.
[invited_character.GetFullName] has arrived at your court, ready for service.
I shall make [invited_character.GetFirstName] a commander.
Excellent
[invited_character.GetFirstName] is not what I asked for, begone!
